thread:
AcmeOps: Hey team — starting ~03:45 UTC our production app started getting a lot of 429s. We think it's tied to multi-region routing. Can someone help triage? We're seeing all traffic routed to eu-west-1 and then spikes of 429s with fallback to us-east-1.

Sara: Thanks for the ping. Do you have example request IDs or a short repro? 429 body message?

AcmeOps: Yep — sample error: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-redwood-request-id: rqd-0a1b2c3d
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
x-redwood-rate-limit: 600/600
body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","detail":"regional capacity exhausted, attempting fallback"}
```

And here's a snippet of our client call (we set region=auto):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"ping","region":"auto","client_request_id":"acme-req-123"}'
```

Mike: Quick question — are you on a Dedicated plan or Hosted? Dedicated pools have reserved capacity per region; Hosted falls back across regions when local capacity is exhausted which can trigger cross-region throttles.

AcmeOps: Hosted. We usually rely on auto region routing for latency.

Ashley: Okay. From the error it looks like eu-west-1 queueing hit a hard limit (x-redwood-rate-limit shows fully used). When that happens our router will backpressure and either queue, reject, or failover depending on the policy. Do you have any tracing headers (x-redwood-request-id) for a batch? We can look at routing logs.

AcmeOps: Gave one above. Here's another chain: rqd-1f2e3d4c, rqd-1f2e3d4d, rqd-1f2e3d4e — many in that minute.

Reza: Pulling logs for those request ids... (repro note: internal logs show route decisions)

InfraBot: route-log rqd-1f2e3d4c -> incoming region=suggested: eu-west-1; route chosen=eu-west-1; decision=reject_quota_exhausted; fallback attempted=us-east-1; fallback_result=accepted; end_status=200 after 850ms

InfraBot: route-log rqd-1f2e3d4d -> incoming region=suggested: eu-west-1; route chosen=eu-west-1; decision=reject_quota_exhausted; fallback attempted=us-east-1; fallback_result=reject_rate_limit; end_status=429; reason=burst_budget_depleted

Sara: That pattern is useful — some requests did successfully failover, others hit cross-region throttles because the destination ran out of burst credits. Are these spikes steady or short bursts?

AcmeOps: They were sudden bursts from a cron job that fan-out 2000 requests in 30s. We've since throttled the cron.

Mike: Two things to consider: 1) For hosted customers we recommend enabling regional affinity with a fallback policy that prefers queueing (if your latency SLO allows) instead of immediate cross-region failover. 2) Increase burst credits or request quota increase for eu-west-1 if this workload is expected.

Ashley: Repro steps we use to simulate:
  - set client region=eu-west-1 explicitly
  - run 2000 concurrent requests at t=0 (eg: hey -n 2000 -c 200)
  - watch request traces 
Look for router decisions in the traces: prefer_queue, reject_quota_exhausted, fallback_attempted.

AcmeOps: Can you share the exact header to force region in the SDK? We do raw HTTP now.

Sara: Use header `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` or the SDK param region: 'eu-west-1'. Example curl: 

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
     -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Reza: Also include `X-Redwood-Client-Request-Id` so we can map traces. If you hit 429s, send us a few request ids and the minute window and we'll pull internal router metrics (queue depth, fallback rate, burst credits).

AcmeOps: Ok will run the explicit-region test and send ids. One more: is there a way to prefer queueing instead of failing over? We want to avoid cross-region latencies and extra costs.

Ashley: Yes. There is a routing policy flag `failover_strategy` in the tenant config (only available on hosted via support change). Options: `immediate_failover` (default for low-latency tiers), `queue_then_failover` (holds up to X ms), `no_failover` (reject locally if region exhausted). We can flip it to `queue_then_failover` with a 500ms cap.

Mike: If you want us to change this for your account, please confirm the tenant id and expected SLO. We'll run it behind a feature flag and monitor for increased tail latency.

AcmeOps: Tenant is acme-123. Our SLO for generation is 400ms p95. Queueing sounds risky. Maybe `no_failover` + smaller retries?

Sara: Understood. We can propose: set `queue_then_failover` 200ms for the next 24h and monitor p95. If you still see 429 amplification due to retries, switch to `no_failover`.

AcmeOps: Sounds good. Please apply and I'll re-run the cron ramp to verify.

InfraBot: change-request logged: CR-8732 by Sara to set routing.failover_strategy=queue_then_failover;queue_ms=200 for tenant acme-123; target rollout 10:05 UTC

Reza: Note — if you plan controlled ramp tests, add exponential backoff jitter client-side and set max_retries=2 to avoid retry storms that exhaust burst credits quickly.

AcmeOps: Will do. Thanks all. Will report back with test ids. :thumbsup:
